newsitem.title: UK: UK's Dorrell details old age care insurance plan.
newsitem.headline: UK's Dorrell details old age care insurance plan.

text.p: Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell on Monday gave details of a plan to encourage people to take out insurance against having to go into long-term care in their old age which will form part of the Conservative manifesto for the upcoming election.
Dorrell said the plan was designed to prevent elderly couples from having to sell most of their assets in order to pay fees at private nursing homes.

"What we are announcing today is more generous support for those who take out insurance to cover this kind of cost for themselves. It is a more generous provision than we have ever had before," he said.
Dorrell told BBC radio that at present the state helps people only when their net assets fall below 16,000 stg.
Under the scheme, if people took out insurance against going into care, the amount of assets protected would increase by 150 stg for ever 100 stg worth of insurance.
Dorrell said the estimated cost to the Treasury would not exceed 200 million stg a year even when the scheme was fully operational.
